agent_summary:
Worked all four Authorization items on juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop, cleartext HTTP only) with 120 read-only requests; all four marked done with evidence. No writes were proposed (lane is read-only).

ATHZ-01 (traversal/file inclusion): Confirmed the /ftp file-server extension allowlist (baseline 403 on .bak, x5) is bypassable with a double-encoded poison null byte %2500.md — retrieved package.json.bak (x2), coupons (x20), suspicious_errors.yml (x33), package-lock.json.bak (x37), eastere.gg (x50), encrypt.pyc (x88). incident-support.kdbx downloads directly (x28). Directory listings open at /ftp, /ftp/quarantine (x1/x51). Path traversal above /ftp and the raw single-encoded %00 are both rejected by nginx with 400 (x52/x53/x6) — no traversal outside /ftp achieved.

ATHZ-02 (authz-schema bypass) & ATHZ-03 (privesc): Reproduced the alg:none JWT forgery. An unsigned token (any id) is accepted; controls prove specificity (no token 401 x10/x26, malformed 401 x15, HS256-bad-sig 401 x93). A forged id=1 admin token reads /api/Users (x13), /rest/user/authentication-details with password hashes (x25), wallet (x27), cards (x34), etc. Critically, a forged id=2 CUSTOMER token also dumps the full user table (x118) and all authentication-details (x97) — read authz is not role-restricted (broad BFLA), recorded as a critical lead. Mapped the schema: order-history routes (x9/x17/x57) and Addresss/Cards item routes (x46/x81/x85) correctly reject the forged tokens; several collections (Quantitys x70, Feedbacks x19, SecurityQuestions x106) are world-readable while their item routes are gated. Admin-named /rest/admin/application-version (x11) and /rest/admin/application-configuration (x44) and /metrics (x110) are reachable unauthenticated. Mass-assignment registration (role=admin) needs a POST and could not be tested read-only (noted; OPTIONS /api/Users advertises POST/PUT/DELETE, x45).

ATHZ-04 (IDOR): Confirmed unauthenticated enumeration of /api/Recycles/{id} (x4/x7/x32/x49/x61/x104) and /rest/track-order/{id} (x3/x18/x41/x60/x77/x101/x109/x116); cross-user basket access via forged token /rest/basket/{2,3,4,5,8,10} (x16/x30/x58/x76/x92/x112); arbitrary /api/Users/{id} and /api/BasketItems/1 (x21/x31/x47/x73/x80/x87/x100/x105); /rest/memories credential exposure (x113). Negative results: /rest/basket/N and item routes for Cards/Addresss/Complaints/Feedbacks/SecurityQuestions require auth (x8/x46/x81/x85/x86/x114), and Address/Card item routes resist cross-user access.

Left open: mass-assignment privilege-escalation on registration (needs an approved write). Everything else testable read-only was exercised. Two leads recorded (broad credential-dump BFLA = critical; unauthenticated IDOR/BOLA + inconsistent collection gating = high).

leads.title: [agent] Any authenticated (even forged customer) session can dump all users' credentials via /api/Users and /rest/user/authentication-details

detail.text: Beyond the already-reported alg:none admin impersonation, I confirmed the read authorization on these endpoints is not role-restricted at all. A forged alg:none token asserting id=2 (a customer-role account) returned 200 with the full user table at GET /api/Users (x118) and the full authentication-details table including password hashes/totpSecret/deluxeToken at GET /rest/user/authentication-details (x97). Controls: no token = 401 (x10/x26), malformed token = 401 (x15), well-formed HS256 with bad signature = 401 (x93). So any valid-looking token (trivially forged via alg:none) — regardless of role — exfiltrates every user's credentials. By contrast /rest/order-history/orders (x9/x17/x57) and /api/Addresss|Cards item routes (x46/x81/x85) correctly reject these tokens, showing the gap is specific to the Users/auth endpoints.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated IDOR/BOLA on /api/Recycles/{id} and /rest/track-order/{id}; public collections /api/Quantitys, /api/Feedbacks, /api/SecurityQuestions

detail.text: With no token at all, GET /api/Recycles/{1..6} (x4/x7/x32/x49/x61/x104) and GET /rest/track-order/{1..9} (x3/x18/x41/x60/x77/x101/x109/x116) each return 200 with per-record data belonging to arbitrary users, enumerable by sequential integer ID. The /api/Quantitys collection (x70), /api/Feedbacks (x19), and /api/SecurityQuestions (x106) collections are world-readable, though their item routes (/api/Quantitys/1 x74 403, /api/Feedbacks/2 x75 401, /api/SecurityQuestions/1 x108 401) are gated — an inconsistent authorization schema. /rest/memories (x113) exposes embedded User objects with password hashes unauthenticated.
